question_text: A 63-year-old woman with a past medical history significant for hypertension presents to the outpatient clinic for evaluation of vaginal dryness, loss of libido, and hot flashes. These symptoms have been progressively worsening over the past 3 months. Her vital signs are: blood pressure 131/81 mm Hg, pulse 68/min, and respiratory rate 16/min. She is afebrile. On further review of systems, she endorses having irregular periods for almost a year, and asks if she has begun menopause. Which of the following parameters is required to formally diagnosis menopause in this patient?

                    ### Question
                    A 63-year-old woman with a past medical history significant for hypertension presents to the outpatient clinic for evaluation of vaginal dryness, loss of libido, and hot flashes. These symptoms have been progressively worsening over the past 3 months. Her vital signs are: blood pressure 131/81 mm Hg, pulse 68/min, and respiratory rate 16/min. She is afebrile. On further review of systems, she endorses having irregular periods for almost a year, and asks if she has begun menopause. Which of the following parameters is required to formally diagnosis menopause in this patient?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Cessation of menses for at least 12 months
opb. Increased serum follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH)
opc. Increased serum luteinizing hormone (LH)
opd. Increased total cholesterol
ope. Pelvic ultrasound demonstrating decreased follicular activity

To formally diagnose menopause in this patient, cessation of menses for at least 12 months is required. Increased serum FSH and LH levels, as well as a pelvic ultrasound demonstrating decreased follicular activity, may support the diagnosis but are not required parameters.
